final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate than a clean-compliance claim, but it still does not satisfy the policy predicate. The admissible evidence shows an underperforming childcare subsidy eligibility segment, that the segment is a named launch use case in two county commitments, and that legal review on disclosure remains unresolved. The governing policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. No admissible evidence shows completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a final legal determination. Because the unresolved predicate remains, this is not merely a caveated-but-compliant case; it remains noncompliant on the present record.
remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the childcare subsidy eligibility segment misses target and is a named launch use case in two county rollout commitments.
Policy states a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality in that circumstance.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering launch without prior resolution.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a required compliance predicate is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public governance guidance do not satisfy the specific disclosure-or-risk-acceptance requirement.
